newsitem.title: ANTIGUA: CRICKET-WEST INDIES WANT WORLD CUP EVERY TWO YEARS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WEST INDIES WANT WORLD CUP EVERY TWO YEARS.

text.p: West Indies want cricket's World Cup to be staged every two years instead of every four years.
Caribbean officials are also seeking to host the 2003 edition of the game's most prestigious limited overs tournament.

The West Indies Cricket Board (WICB) is to meet here on Saturday to finalise plans for its bid, ahead of an International Cricket Council (ICC) meeting in Malaysia next month, said board secretary Andrew Sealy.
England are hosting the next World Cup in 1999 and South Africa have been awarded the 2003 event, although the West Indies are still challenging for it.
They are also pushing to host an earlier World Cup if the ICC approves a proposal to have the tournament every two years instead of every four.
Sealy said on the Caribbean News Agency's (CANA) radio sports programme on Tuesday: "The West Indies have a two-fold attack basically.

"We feel that we are entitled to the World Cup in 2003.... but outside of that fact, we are also keen to have the World Cup changed from every four years to every two years, and we are suggesting that 2001 is when the next World Cup could be held after 1999."
At the ICC meeting in Malaysia, the WICB's position will be put forward by president Pat Rousseau, vice-president Julian Hunte and chief executive officer Steve Camacho.
The WICB is "cautiously optimistic" the final decision over the 2003 venue - not expected until the traditional full ICC meeting at Lord's in July - will be in its favour.
Sealy said West Indies' proposal to host the World Cup would feature a strong effort from various facets of the region and must not be seen as purely a WICB venture.
The last World Cup was held in India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka 12 months ago, and won by Sri Lanka.
